alerts.title: Carbamazepine contraindicated with DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines list carbamazepine as a contraindication for DTG, and state it decreases DTG levels by 30–70%. The patient started carbamazepine 2 weeks ago while on DTG. Viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence, consistent with subtherapeutic DTG levels. Guidelines recommend using valproic acid instead. The clinician's plan to reduce carbamazepine dose does not address the interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Discontinue carbamazepine and use valproic acid for seizure management as per guidelines. Repeat viral load after switching.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatremia
alerts.message: Patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12), hyponatremia (Na 128 mmol/L), nystagmus, ataxia, and tremor. Carbamazepine is a known cause of SIADH and hyponatremia. Valproate may also contribute to hyponatremia. The clinician plans dose reduction and repeat level, which is appropriate. Sodium should be monitored closely and corrected as needed.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, repeat level and sodium. Consider switching to valproic acid monotherapy to eliminate the DTG interaction.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load needs adherence review
alerts.message: Guidelines state a repeat viral load >1000 copies/mL suggests treatment failure, requiring HIV drug resistance testing and switch after ruling out adherence issues. This patient's VL of 1,240 copies/mL exceeds that threshold. The likely cause is the carbamazepine–DTG interaction reducing DTG levels, but the clinician's plan does not address the VL or outline next steps for resistance testing or regimen review.

evidence.recommended_action: Address the carbamazepine–DTG interaction first. Repeat viral load after correction; if still >1000, proceed to HIV drug resistance testing.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT with hepatotoxic drugs
alerts.message: ALT is 68 U/L. Both carbamazepine and valproate can cause hepatotoxicity; TDF has also been associated with liver enzyme derangement. Guidelines recommend LFTs and RFTs when TDF-related toxicity is suspected. The combination of two hepatotoxic anticonvulsants plus TDF compounds risk. Non-drug causes should also be considered. The clinician's plan does not include ALT follow-up.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat ALT after carbamazepine dose adjustment. If persistently elevated, evaluate for drug-induced liver injury and consider regimen review.
